data.title: Žilina-Závodie – a refuge hillfort above Strážov
data.excerpt: The hillfort at spot height 626 above Žilina-Závodie covers some 6 hectares and its ramparts still reach over three metres in places, yet it yielded almost no finds apart from a few sherds of the Púchov culture. It was a refuge for the population of the surrounding settlements — from the Late and Final Bronze Age, through the Late La Tène period, to the High Middle Ages — and Matej Bel already described it in his work on Trenčín County.
data.metaTitle: Žilina-Závodie – a hillfort described by Matej Bel
data.metaDescription: The hillfort at spot height 626 in Žilina-Závodie: about 6 ha, ramparts over three metres high, and a mention by Matej Bel in his work on Trenčín County.

children.text: This interesting hillfort of Žilina lies at spot height 626 in the cadastral area of the Závodie district. It is first mentioned as early as in the work of Matej Bel on Trenčín County (Bel 2013, 53), where he states: “The hillfort is overgrown not so much with trees as with dense thickets. It rises from below Žilina in the direction of Hričov. In these heights a castle was once built, and this hill took its name from it. Its ruins still tower today near the village of Strážov”. A contribution by R. Zaymus in the Sborník Muzeálnej slovenskej spoločnosti of 1900, p. 55, also discusses the hillfort, and V. Chaloupecký mentions it in Staré Slovensko (Chaloupecký 1923, 94).

children.text: The fortification has thus been known for a long time. By cadastral area it belongs to Závodie, but geographically rather to Strážov. The whole summit is surrounded by a stony-loamy rampart, which is most massive above the most accessible position and lower above the adjoining bailey, whose fortification takes the form of no more than a kind of terrace. R. Marsina supposed that the fortification of Hradisko was of Slavic origin, but the trial excavation by G. Povala in 1964 produced only sherds of the Púchov culture and, in a small barrow-like feature, similar pottery (fig. 6). This may have been a cremation grave under a small barrow mound. The shallow saddle between Hradisko and the neighbouring spot height 632 is called Medzihradné. The name draws attention to the possibility that there may have been a fortification — perhaps only of timber — on spot height 632 as well.

Access to the Žilina Basin was guarded by the fortifications of Divinka Veľký vrch, Háj above Divinka, Chlmecký vrch, Zámčisko at Žilinská Lehota, Háj above Ovčiarsko and Hradisko above Strážov. This too speaks of the important position of Žilina and of its early occupation, represented by extensive settlements at the localities of Frambor, Šefranica, in Závodie at Pod Vinicou and Pod Skalkou, in Bánová, in Strážov – especially the locality of Tomanová. And many others in the surrounding villages – Bánová, Bitarová, Hôrky, Ovčiarsko.

Hradisko above Strážov was only a refuge – that is, a refuge fortification where the local population sheltered only in times of danger. The most intensive occupation is attested, as in the case of Straník, above all for the period of the Late to Final Bronze Age, then for the period of the Late La Tène to the Early Roman period, and finally for the Slavic period, from the turn of the 5th and 6th centuries to the High Middle Ages. In all these horizons it evidently served to protect the population of the surrounding settlements, concentrated in the vicinity of Hradisko.

children.text:
The hillfort at Závodie, with its area of about 6 ha, is similar to the hillfort on Straník. Only the rampart fortification here is far more pronounced and in places the height of the ramparts reaches over three metres. The access to the fortified enclosure is on the southern side and it may be assumed that it was protected by a gateway, as was customary at fortifications of this kind. Finds from the area of the hillfort are unfortunately almost non-existent, apart from those few sherds of the Púchov culture. For this reason it is also very difficult to date the construction of the fortification. We have to proceed only from the find situation of the surrounding settlements, which are most strongly represented above all in the Late to Final Bronze Age and then in the period around the change of the eras, when the people of the Púchov culture lived here. That was evidently when the greatest opportunity existed to build such massive ramparts over so large an area. The people of the Lusatian and of the Púchov cultures were decisively responsible for the creation of the great Hradisko above Závodie, which even today is a popular destination for the excursions of local inhabitants.
 
 Text by: Mgr. Jozef Moravčík
